proof_contracts: Finite S and nonempty finite A(s), bounded rewards, stochastic rows, beta in (0,1); histories and randomized policies specified. Prove contraction through finite maxima, Cauchy iteration, all-history finite-horizon/tail identification and stationary maximizing-policy attainment.

Policy value is the nonnegative geometric inverse; greedy improvement is monotone and strict at a changed state under incumbent tie retention. Finite policies imply termination. True residual bounds value error and approximate-greedy policy loss; operator error must be added explicitly.

Finite exogenous shock tree, adapted nonnegative scalar capital, increasing concave differentiable utility/technology and strictly positive candidate consumption. Local two-date perturbations yield conditional Euler equality or lower/upper inequalities. Concavity plus conditional tower cancellation and expected shadow-value tail give sufficiency against every integrable adapted feasible path; general TVC necessity is not asserted.

Log/Cobb example has unbounded-below rewards and open actions. Prove feasibility, bounded positive utility parts, explicit finite candidate value, global stage maximization, Euler and vanishing tail separately from the finite-state theorem.
Existence/attainment and approximation boundaries receive explicit nonattainment, omitted-state, overaccumulation and false-residual witnesses.

cases.title: A cash state that forgets readiness
cases.inputs: One final date: observed readiness h=0/1 with probability half, cash 2; setup costs 3/1 paid before production receipt 3. No borrowing; idle keeps cash.
cases.point: Current information changes feasibility; averaging setup costs cannot finance the cold history.

cases.title: A small complete control model
cases.inputs: State 0 actions wait:(reward1,next0), repair:(−1,next1); state1 harvest:(4,next0), maintain:(2,next1). beta=3/4. Rewards are utility, not a financing promise.

anchors.discount_switch: 2/3; all four policies tie at equality

cases.point: Enumeration, policy improvement and residual calculations agree; no general physical-path convergence is inferred.

cases.title: Unbounded log growth verified without the wrong norm
cases.point: Constructed policy and full shadow-tail proof establish optimum; bounded-reward contraction is not applied.

cases.title: A borrowing corner and a mean-income shortcut
cases.inputs: Two dates, log utility,beta=1/2,R=1, terminal income1/4 with equal weights; nonnegative saving a<m. Compare endowed wealth2 and4.
cases.point: Strict concavity proves global optimum and the expectation of marginal utility cannot be replaced by marginal utility at mean income.

cases.title: Euler holds while valuable resources are abandoned
cases.point: All constant Euler-feasible consumption c in (0,2] can be characterized; only c=2 exhausts the intertemporal budget.

cases.title: Which residual did the solver measure?
cases.inputs: Baseline finite Bellman T versus Ttilde=T+1/20; separately one-state true actions reward0/1 with beta3/4 but coarse action list includes only0.
cases.point: A solver can converge exactly to a different problem; error certification needs a true-operator or verified operator-difference bound.

exercise_routes.task: Specify the missing state and admissible actions; compute observed and blind funded values.
Prove all-history finite-horizon induction and discounted tail bound for the finite MDP.
Evaluate all four policies and perform incumbent-retaining policy iteration; change repair success to3/4 and rederive value and threshold.
Derive every optimal stationary policy on both sides of beta2/3 and at equality.
Prove the full VI formula from n2, its exact residual/error and the first n achieving value error≤1/10.
Prove the approximation residual certificate and reconstruct both false-zero-residual cases.
Derive the general log value constants/policy, then verify the original numeric path and global tail sufficiency.
Derive conditional Euler equality/inequalities by an adapted perturbation; include a terminal salvage transfer with log(1+k′).
Derive the risky two-date saving boundary and radical interior root, then show why mean income changes the decision.
Characterize the entire constant-consumption Euler family and prove the unique optimal member with a present-value budget.
One-state actions[0,1), reward a,beta3/4: prove contraction and value4 but no policy attains; supply epsilon policies.
Referee a converged-grid/Euler/automatic-state/stationarity claim; use exact witnesses and specify the minimum valid validation evidence.

seed_evidence.scope: Exact rational two-state policy/VI reconstruction; radical Euler substitution; log value and steady-policy formulas independently derived. This is prototype evidence, not a final runtime gate.

limits: No general Borel-state measurable-selection theorem, arbitrary unbounded-reward contraction, universal TVC necessity, empirical calibration or distributional equilibrium existence is claimed.
